You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as A-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: Egwi (Etche LGA)
Curve type: A-type (ρ1 < ρ2 < ρ3 < ρ4 < ρ5: 295.9 < 798.6 < 864.6 < 1810.2 < 5634.2 ohm-m) — resistivity increases monotonically with depth, no conductive clay horizon detected in the sounded section.
Aquifer depth: ~6.3 m to ~44.3 m — the thick (37.96 m) 1810 ohm-m fourth layer, interpreted as coarse sand/gravel. (Note: the tabulated "depth to base = 37.25 m" is inconsistent with 6.2935 + 37.957 = 44.25 m; treat 44.25 m as the base and confirm against the raw inversion before setting casing depths.)
Recommendation: Drill to about 50 m to fully penetrate the fourth layer and terminate just inside the underlying very high-resistivity unit, screening the interval from roughly 15 m to 44 m where saturation is most likely, and log cuttings continuously to pick the true static water level since the A-type curve gives no resistivity contrast to mark the water table. Because there is no overlying clay aquitard, the aquifer is unconfined and vulnerable to surface pollution — case and grout a sanitary seal through the full upper 6 m and site the borehole well away from pit latrines, soakaways and fuel storage.
